function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Sure! Building a complete Trucking Transportation Management System (TMS) is a big undertaking—there’s routing & scheduling, load management, fleet tracking, invoicing, analytics, integrations with GPS/GIS services, APIs for carriers, mobile apps, dashboards, security/authentication, database design, deployment pipelines, etc. Below I’ll outline a **high‑level architecture** and then give you a minimal, modular starter project written in **Python + FastAPI** (backend), **React** (frontend), and **PostgreSQL** (database). You can extend each component as your needs grow. --- ## 📦 Project Overview | Layer | Tech Stack | Responsibility | |-------|------------|----------------| | **Backend** | FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + PostgreSQL | RESTful API, business logic, auth, DB access | | **Frontend** | React + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS | UI / UX, forms, maps, charts | | **Auth** | OAuth2 JWT + Password Hashing | Secure login, role-based permissions | | **Routing Engine** | OR-tools (Google) or GraphHopper | Optimize routes, calculate ETA | | **Fleet Tracking** | WebSocket + Socket.io | Real‑time vehicle telemetry | | **Data Storage** | TimescaleDB extension on Postgres | Time-series logs (location history) | | **Deployment** | Docker Compose + Kubernetes (optional) | Containerized microservices | > ⚠️ *This is just a starting point.* > For production use, add proper logging, monitoring (Prometheus+Grafana), CI/CD, automated tests, backup strategies, compliance checks, etc. --- ## 🗂️ Directory Structure ``` tms/ ├── backend/ │ ├─ app/ │ │ ├─ main.py # FastAPI entrypoint │ │ ├─ models.py # ORM entities │ │ ├─ schemas.py # Pydantic DTOs │ │ ├─ crud.py # CRUD helpers │ │ ├─ routers/ │ │ │ ├─ users.py │ │ │ ├─ trucks.py │ │ │ └─ loads.py │ │ ├─ deps.py # Dependencies (db sessions, auth) │ │ └─ utils.py # Helpers (hashing, email, etc.) │ ├─ alembic/ # Database migrations │ ├─ dockerfile # Backend image │ └─ .env.example └── frontend/ ├─ src/ │ ├─ components/ │ ├─ pages/ │ ├─ hooks/ │ ├─ api.ts # Axios instance │ └─ App.tsx ├─ public/ ├─ tailwind.config.js ├─ package.json └─ tsconfig.json ``` --- ## 🚀 Quick Start Guide ### Prerequisites ```bash docker-compose --version python -m venv env && source env/bin/activate pip install poetry ``` #### 1️⃣ Spin Up Services ```bash cd tms/backend poetry install alembic upgrade head # Create tables cd ../.. docker compose up -d ``` Your API will now run at `http://localhost:8000` and Swagger docs at `/docs`. #### 2️⃣ Seed Data (Optional) Create a superadmin: ```bash curl -XPOST http://localhost:8000/users/register \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"email": "admin@example.com", "password": "StrongPass123!", "role": "ADMIN"}' ``` Login to get a JWT: ```bash curl -XPOST http://localhost:8000/token \ -F username=admin@example.com \ -F password=StrongPass123! ``` Use this token (`Authorization: Bearer `) when calling protected endpoints. --- ## 🔧 Core Code Snippets ### 1️⃣ FastAPI Main File – `app/main.py` ```python from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends from sqlalchemy.orm import Session import uvicorn from .routers import users, trucks, loads from .deps import get_db, oauth2_scheme from .models import Base, engine Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine) app = FastAPI(title="Trucking TMS") @app.get("/") def read_root(): return {"message": "Welcome to the Trucking TMS"} app.include_router(users.router, prefix="/users") app.include_router(trucks.router, prefix="/trucks") app.include_router(loads.router, prefix="/loads") if __name__ == "__main__": uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000) ``` ### 2️⃣ User Router – `app/routers/users.py` ```python from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, status, HTTPException from pydantic import EmailStr from typing import List from ..schemas import UserIn, UserOut, Token from ..crud import create_user, authenticate_user, get_users from ..utils import hash_password, verify_password from ..deps import get_db, get_current_active_admin router = APIRouter() @router.post("/register", response_model=UserOut, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED) async def register(user_in: UserIn, db: Session = Depends(get_db)): hashed_pw = hash_password(user_in.password) new_user = await create_user(db=db, user=user_in.copy(update={"hashed_password": hashed_pw})) return new_user @router.post("/login", response_model=Token) async def login(form_data: dict): # Use OAuth2PasswordRequestForm if using form encoding ... @router.get("/", response_model=List[UserOut], dependencies=[Depends(get_current_active_admin)]) async def list_users(skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100, db: Session = Depends(get_db)): return await get_users(db, skip=skip, limit=limit) ``` *(CRUD operations follow standard patterns.)* ### 3️⃣ Routing Optimization Example – `app/utils/routing.py` ```python import googlemaps from datetime import timedelta gmaps_client = googlemaps.Client(key=os.getenv("GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY")) def optimize_route(locations: List[str]) -> Dict: """ Uses Google Maps Directions API to compute optimal route. :param locations: Ordered list of addresses or lat/lng strings. :return: JSON containing optimized order, total distance, duration. """ result = gmaps_client.directions( origin=locations[0], destination=locations[-1], waypoints=locations[1:-1] if len(locations)>2 else None, mode='driving', departure_time=datetime.utcnow(), traffic_model='best_guess', avoid=['ferries', 'indoor'], alternatives=False, units='metric', region='us', optimization=True ) return result[0] ``` *Note:* Replace with open-source libraries like [OR-Tools](https://developers.google.com/optimization/) if you prefer not to rely on external paid APIs. ### 4️⃣ Frontend Sample Component – `src/pages/Dashboard.tsx` ```tsx import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'; import axiosInstance from '../api'; interface Load { id: number; pickupAddress: string; deliveryAddress: string; weightKg: number; } export const Dashboard = () => { const [loads, setLoads] = useState([]); useEffect(() => { async function fetchLoads() { try { const res = await axiosInstance.get('/loads'); setLoads(res.data); } catch (err) { console.error(err); } } fetchLoads(); }, []); return (

Active Loads

{/* Table headers */} {loads.map((load) => ( ))}
{load.pickupAddress} {load.deliveryAddress} {load.weightKg} kg
); }; ``` --- ## 🎯 Next Steps & Enhancements | Feature | Suggested Implementation | |---------|--------------------------| | **Real-time Fleet Tracking** | Publish MQTT topics per truck → Subscribe via WebSockets to update map markers live. | | **Geofencing Alerts** | Store geofence polygons in PostGIS; trigger alerts when vehicles cross boundaries. | | **Dynamic Pricing** | Integrate fuel price feeds; adjust freight rates accordingly. | | **Analytics Dashboards** | Grafana connected to TimescaleDB for KPI visualizations. | | **Mobile Apps** | Build native iOS/Android clients using Flutter or React Native. | | **Carrier Marketplace** | Expose marketplace APIs so third-party carriers can bid on loads. | | **Compliance Checks** | Validate driver hours-of-service against FMCSA regulations automatically. | Feel free to let me know which part you'd like deeper help with—whether that's setting up the database schema, writing specific API endpoints, integrating a particular routing library, or anything else. Happy coding!
